biggestGap: No fruit is identifiable by its outline: over 32 uniform-SO(3) orientations of the shipping geometry the watermelon, orange, kiwi and apple BODIES all fall inside one band (elongation 1.21-1.36, boundary cv 0.078-0.130) and the between-species silhouette distance is 0.91-1.18x the within-species distance, so two random views of the same fruit differ as much as two different fruits.
evidence: PREDECESSOR'S PROBES REPRODUCED EXACTLY (max-channel luminance, threshold 8, largest connected component, 720-ray radial trace from the bbox centre, residual above a k<=3 low-pass fit). r3/01-whole-watermelon: bbox 144x131, aspect 1.099, cv 0.1054, k<=3 max protrusion 7.86% (r4 critic quoted 144x131 / 1.099 / 0.1052 / 7.6% - reproduced). r4/01-whole: 157x157, aspect 1.000, cv 0.0855, max protrusion 5.38%. r4b/01-whole: 122x148, aspect 0.824, cv 0.1695, max protrusion 8.56%, and above a least-squares ELLIPSE fit (the orchestrator's probe) 24.4% vs r4's 10.6%. THE ORIENTATION FIX HELD ON r5 - trivially: shots/r5/01-whole-watermelon.png is BYTE-IDENTICAL to shots/r4b (md5 match; it is the only one of the 16 shots that is), so 0.824 / 0.1695 / 8.56% / 24.4% carry over unchanged and the r4 blockers (aspect 1.000, protrusion 5.4%) are genuinely gone. The r5 geometry work is also real and matches its report: I rebuilt makeFruitGeometry(SPECIES[id], 9) in node and get 2708/2434/1760/2668 tris for melon/orange/kiwi/apple (bit-identical to r4 as claimed) and 6412 for the pineapple (report 6412, r4 7516, -14.7%). NOW THE ASSIGNED QUESTION, ANSWERED NO. I wrote an orthographic silhouette rasteriser (320^2, 32 uniform-SO(3) orientations, 360-ray trace, rotation-invariant descriptors) against the shipping geometry. Median elongation (ratio of the k=2 harmonic fit's major to minor axis): watermelon 1.363, orange 1.208, kiwi 1.222, apple 1.225, strawberry 1.094, pineapple 1.867. Median boundary cv: 0.130 / 0.082 / 0.078 / 0.130 / 0.129 / 0.291. Orange and kiwi are the SAME BODY to two decimals - and both are wrong in opposite directions, since a real orange is round (1.00) and a real kiwi is a 1.5:1 prolate barrel. Angular fraction of the limb carrying >10% protrusion above a k<=3 fit: orange 0.0%, kiwi 0.0%, watermelon 3.1%, apple 3.9% (so the apple's headline 39.4% peak residual is a 1-px needle over 3.9% of the boundary, not a readable stem), strawberry 12.6%, pineapple 14.0%. Best-rotation, flip-invariant RMS distance between normalised radial signatures: nearest-other-species / within-species = 1.03 melon, 0.97 orange, 1.18 kiwi, 0.91 apple, 0.94 strawberry, 1.06 pineapple. That ratio is CONSERVATIVE in the build's favour, because my within-class set contains near-duplicate adjacent orientations that depress the denominator, and it still sits at 1.0. A 1-NN leave-one-out scores 81.8%, but the confusion matrix shows it is only picking a neighbouring view of the same object; it is not identity. THE EYE AGREES: I built a 6x5 unlabelled binary contact sheet from that rasteriser (tools/critic5/geo-sheet.png) and rows 1-3 - watermelon, orange, kiwi - are unsortable; they are the same lumpy ball five times over. Row 4 (apple) is that ball plus one hair spike. Row 5 (strawberry) is a crumpled paper ball with no cone and no calyx star. Row 6 (pineapple) reads as a hedgehog / shuttlecock, not a pineapple. Same test on the DELIVERED frames (silhouettes cut from shots/r5/01, 07, 08, 11, 12; tools/critic5/sheet2.png): circularity 1.02 orange / 1.00 kiwi / 1.06 apple / 0.91 strawberry, hf(k=6..60) boundary energy 0.023 / 0.022 / 0.026 / 0.035 - four interchangeable lozenges. Against plate-01 that is the whole game: the plate's strawberry is a heart with a pointed apex and a five-pointed sepal star, its kiwi is a truncated cylinder with a flat cut end, its pineapple is ~12 broad sword leaves each as long as the body arching up in a rosette. Ours are a ball, a ball, and a 180-degree spray of thin spikes several of which point downward. Blind on shots/r5/09-combo+50ms.png or 00-hero.png against plate-01: instant, under a second. Scale is no longer the auto-fail it was - the hero melon measures 327 px of 720 = 45.4% of frame height (r4 crop 44.3%), above the 25% floor though still short of the plate's ~55-62%. Perf holds: 129 draw calls, 215606 tris, cpu median 0.1 / p95 0.5 ms, zero errors.
